page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor running at 2.25 GHz. It delivers 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent block data.

Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps, supporting high-throughput inter-node data exchange. Due to the lack of bundled local NVMe disks, I/O performance relies on external storage volumes, which introduces architectural considerations for latency-sensitive storage designs. The allocation of dedicated vCPUs provides deterministic execution free from hyper-thread contention or noisy-neighbor interference common in shared environments.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:2 memory ratio targets workloads dominated by compute processing rather than memory footprint. This configuration suits distributed computing, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, web application server fleets, and computational modeling where 64 dedicated processing threads can be fully saturated without paying for excess RAM capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9ae.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T95 processor clocked at 2.25 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 compute profile with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes with no integrated GPU hardware and lacks local storage, depending on external storage infrastructure for operating system and data volumes. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps, providing substantial throughput for distributed architectures. The high core count combined with dedicated processing threads makes this instance well matched for parallel batch compute, video transcoding, continuous integration and build systems, web serving clusters, and computational simulation workloads that require intensive CPU processing without high memory overhead per core.
